findings.title: Unparenthesized OR filter can break the AND composition when it is the first and only condition
Empty teamIds array makes the org condition cast ambiguous
Constructor accepts a loosened public options type that bypasses schema validation
Tests lost caching coverage and assert on SQL internals

response:
## 1) Severity: HIGH | Type: Bug
Title: Unparenthesized OR filter can break the AND composition when it is the first and only condition

Affected:
- packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:104-123

Explanation:
`buildFilterConditions` returns `("eventTypeId" = X) OR ("eventParentId" = X)` without outer parentheses when it is the only condition. A caller that embeds the result in a larger SQL string with its own AND, without wrapping it, gets the wrong precedence and leaks rows. `getBaseConditions` does wrap it, but `getFilterConditions` is public and may be used on its own. `buildAuthorizationConditions` has the same problem: its OR expression is returned unwrapped. Wrap each returned fragment in parentheses.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
conditions.push(Prisma.sql`(("eventTypeId" = ${id}) OR ("eventParentId" = ${id}))`);
// and wrap the returned org/team auth OR expressions: Prisma.sql`(${expr})`
~~~

## 2) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Empty teamIds array makes the org condition cast ambiguous

Affected:
- packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:164

Explanation:
`"teamId" = ANY(${teamIds})` is passed as a bound parameter. If `teamIds` is empty, Prisma may serialize it in a way that Postgres cannot type, which can cause a runtime error such as "cannot determine type of empty array". The user-ID branch guards against an empty array, but the team branch does not. Guard against empty arrays, or cast explicitly with `::int[]`.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
Prisma.sql`("teamId" = ANY(${teamIds}::int[])) AND ("isTeamBooking" = true)`
~~~

## 3) Severity: LOW | Type: Maintainability
Title: Constructor accepts a loosened public options type that bypasses schema validation

Affected:
- packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:29-34
- packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:58

Explanation:
`InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` is a loose type, not a discriminated union. It allows `scope: "team"` without a `teamId`. The constructor presumably validates it with zod, and invalid input then silently yields `options = null` and the NOTHING condition. Callers get no compile-time feedback. Use a discriminated-union type instead.

## 4) Severity: LOW | Type: Test
Title: Tests lost caching coverage and assert on SQL internals

Affected:
- packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:429-431

Explanation:
The caching tests were removed even though caching logic remains in the service. Most remaining tests compare exact `Prisma.sql` template structure, so they break on harmless formatting changes. Only one test actually runs the SQL against the database. Restore the caching tests and add execution-based assertions for the org and team scopes.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In getBaseConditions(), the else if (filterConditions) and final else branches are unreachable. This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.

Fetching userIdsFromOrg only when teamsFromOrg.length > 0 can exclude org-level members for orgs without child teams; consider deriving from teamIds (which includes orgId) or removing the guard so org-only orgs still include member user bookings.
